computation_or_rationale: Participant loans are reported as notes receivable from participants at unpaid principal plus accrued unpaid interest (ASU 2010-25; ASC 962-310), not as investments.
Benefits paid to participants are the main deduction; rollovers and appreciation are additions; a contribution receivable is an asset (its offset is an addition).

DB plans (ASC 960) also report the actuarial present value of accumulated plan benefits and changes in it; DC plans do not. (Option wording says 'actuarial value' - should be 'actuarial present value'.)
ASC 962-205: statement of net assets available for benefits and statement of changes in net assets available for benefits.
8,000,000 + 1,100,000 + 640,000 - 900,000 - 40,000 = 8,800,000. (a) 9,740,000 ignores both deductions; (c) 8,840,000 ignores admin expenses; (d) 8,160,000 omits investment income.
ASC 962-325-35: plan investments at fair value (contract value only for fully benefit-responsive investment contracts).
ASC 960-20: accumulated plan benefits attributable to service already rendered, based on plan provisions; generally no future salary projection (unless plan provisions require).
Accrual basis: contributions receivable recognized for amounts due under plan/formal commitment; record receivable and addition of 75,000.
300,000 - 450,000 = -150,000 net depreciation; realized and unrealized combined as net appreciation/depreciation in FV (ASC 960/962-205-45).
ASC 960-20-50: disclose significant effects of plan amendments, changes in nature of plan, changes in actuarial assumptions.
5,200,000 + 180,000 + 40,000 - 15,000 = 5,405,000. (b) 5,420,000 ignores accrued expenses; (c) 5,225,000 excludes participant loans; (d) 5,185,000 excludes both receivables.
The plan is a separate reporting entity (ASC 960/962/965); sponsor's ASC 715 accounting is separate.
ASC 960-205-45: accumulated plan benefit information may be as of beginning or end of plan year.
ASC 960-205-10: DB plan statements include statement of net assets available for benefits; no cash flow statement required (encouraged only in some cases).
